mainTopic: The 'light prohibition' of אשת איש, and the different explanations of רבי יוסי's rule 'whoever disqualifies others disqualifies himself'
overview: The גמרא finishes explaining a ברייתא that used a קל וחומר. רבא, רבי יוחנן and a ברייתא from אבא חנן all say the 'light prohibition' there is אשת איש. It is called 'light' only because the husband can end it. The פסוק 'אותה' then blocks the קל וחומר: a man who sleeps with his wife's sister does not make his wife forbidden to him. Next the גמרא asks what רבי יוסי meant by 'whoever disqualifies others disqualifies himself.' Two simple guesses fail on the wording. רבי אמי then ties the rule to remarrying by permission of the בית דין versus based on עדים, and רבי יצחק נפחא ties it to a full wife versus a betrothed woman. שמואל rules like רבי יוסי, and רב יוסף objects from שמואל's view about a יבמה. אביי begins answering that שמואל may have meant a different reading or only part of the rule, and his answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבא: the light prohibition is a married woman
steps.stepSummary: רבא sets aside the earlier reading and says the 'light prohibition' in the ברייתא is אשת איש. רבין reports that רבי יוחנן said the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: it means a married woman. And so too, when רבין came, he said in the name of רבי יוחנן: a married woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The word אלא tells us the earlier explanation is dropped. רבא gives a new answer: the 'light prohibition' in the ברייתא means אשת איש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא built its קל וחומר on some 'איסור קל,' and the גמרא needed to know which prohibition that was. רבא now names it as אשת איש. רבין then reports that רבי יוחנן in ארץ ישראל said exactly the same, which gives רבא's answer a second strong voice.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; this drops the earlier idea
When רבין came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said: a married woman.
phrases.notes: He means the 'light prohibition' the ברייתא talked about is a married woman.

phrases.english: And similarly, when Ravin came,
he said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said: a married woman.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the earlier explanation of 'איסור קל' from the previous discussion.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which prohibition does the ברייתא call 'light'?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אשת איש, according to רבא and רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: Why call a married woman a light prohibition
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how אשת איש, a very serious sin, could be called 'light.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And why does the ברייתא call it a 'light prohibition'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks an obvious question about רבא's answer. This line sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אשת איש is one of the gravest איסורים, so calling it 'קל' sounds strange. The גמרא needs to show that 'light' here describes one specific feature, not how bad the sin is.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Light' here does not mean that sleeping with a married woman is a minor sin. It describes one technical feature of the prohibition, which the next step explains.

phrases.english: And why does he call it 'a light prohibition'?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי קָרֵי לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording in light of רבא's answer.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: In what way is אשת איש 'light'?

steps.title: The prohibition does not last all his life
steps.stepSummary: It is 'light' because the husband, whose marriage makes her forbidden to others, does not make her forbidden for his whole life.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the one who makes her forbidden does not make her forbidden for all his days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the איסור of אשת איש can come to an end, so in that one way it is 'light.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband is 'האוסרה,' the one whose marriage makes her forbidden to other men. That איסור can end during his lifetime, for example through a גט. A prohibition that can end is called 'light' compared to one that lasts for a whole lifetime.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who makes her forbidden
All his days; his whole life

phrases.english: Because the one who renders her forbidden does not render her forbidden all his days.
phrases.notes: That's her husband. He can end the איסור, for example by giving her a גט.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁאֵין הָאוֹסְרָהּ אוֹסְרָהּ כׇּל יָמָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is light because the איסור is not permanent.

steps.title: A ברייתא from אבא חנן supports this
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records אבא חנן, in the name of רבי אלעזר, also saying the light prohibition is אשת איש.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way: אבא חנן said in the name of רבי אלעזר: a married woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says the same thing as רבא. This backs up his answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far רבא's reading had the support of אמוראים, רבי יוחנן among them. Now a תנא source, אבא חנן quoting רבי אלעזר, says the same. That makes the reading 'אשת איש' even stronger.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way in a ברייתא

steps.whatToRemember: The 'איסור קל' in the ברייתא is אשת איש. It is called 'light' only because the איסור can end, and רבא, רבי יוחנן and אבא חנן all agree.

phrases.english: It is also taught so:

phrases.aramaic: אַבָּא חָנָן אָמַר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר:
phrases.english: Abba Ḥanan said in the name of Rabbi Elazar:
a married woman.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא נָמֵי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבא's answer with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: The reading that the 'איסור קל' is אשת איש
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: אבא חנן in the name of רבי אלעזר

steps.title: The ברייתא's קל וחומר read with this meaning
steps.stepSummary: With 'light' meaning אשת איש, the ברייתא argues: if a married woman who sins becomes forbidden to her husband, then a man who sleeps with his wife's sister should make his wife forbidden to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: If in the case of one who sleeps with a light איסור, where the one who forbids her does not forbid her all his days, the one who forbids becomes forbidden, then one who sleeps with a severe איסור, where the one who forbids her forbids her all her days, is it not logical that the one who forbids her becomes forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the ברייתא's קל וחומר and reads it with the new meaning. It tries to prove that the wife should become forbidden to her husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Light case: in אשת איש, after she sins, the husband becomes forbidden to her. Severe case: his wife forbids her sister to him for the wife's whole lifetime. So the קל וחומר argues that the wife, who is 'האוסרה' in that case, should become forbidden to him when he sleeps with her sister.

keyTerms.meaning: If in this case... (the opening of a קל וחומר)

steps.confusionAlert: 'האוסרה' points to a different person in each half. In the light case it is the husband. In the severe case it is the wife, who makes her sister forbidden to him.

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה בִּמְקוֹם הַבָּא עַל אִיסּוּר קַל,
phrases.english: And if in a case of one who has relations with a light prohibition,
phrases.notes: This is the married woman case from step 1.

phrases.english: where the one who forbids her does not forbid her all his days,
the one who forbids becomes forbidden,
phrases.notes: After she sins, her husband becomes forbidden to her.

phrases.english: then one who has relations with a severe prohibition,
phrases.notes: This means his wife's sister.

phrases.english: where the one who forbids her forbids her all her days,
is it not logical that the one who forbids her becomes forbidden?
phrases.notes: So his wife should become forbidden to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמָה בִּמְקוֹם הַבָּא עַל אִיסּוּר קַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the definition from steps 1-3 to reread the ברייתא's argument.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that sleeping with his wife's sister does not make his wife forbidden to him
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר from אשת איש (light) to a wife's sister (severe).

steps.title: The פסוק 'אותה' blocks the קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: The word 'אותה' teaches that only a woman's own relations make her forbidden, not her sister's relations.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'her': her own lying with another man forbids her, but her sister's lying does not forbid her.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא knocks down its own קל וחומר with a word in the פסוק. The wife stays permitted to her husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about a סוטה says 'ושכב איש אותה,' 'a man lay with her.' The word 'אותה' limits the איסור to a woman who herself was with another man. The קל וחומר fails because the תורה itself narrows the rule.
steps.whatToRemember: A man who sleeps with his wife's sister does not make his wife forbidden to him. The קל וחומר is blocked by 'אותה': only the wife's own act forbids her.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the הלכה that his wife stays permitted to him even after he sins with her sister.

phrases.english: The verse states: 'her',
phrases.notes: במדבר ה:יג

phrases.english: 'her': her own intercourse renders her forbidden,
but the intercourse of her sister does not render her forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״אוֹתָהּ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the קל וחומר of step 5.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוק limits the איסור to the woman's own act, so logic cannot extend it.

steps.title: Quoting רבי יוסי from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יוסי's rule in the משנה: whoever disqualifies others also disqualifies himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: Whoever disqualifies, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic. It quotes רבי יוסי's words from the משנה so it can explain them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי יוסי said: whoever makes others' wives forbidden to them also makes his own wife forbidden, and whoever does not, does not. 'וכו׳' tells us the rest of his words are known from the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: And so on (the rest of the quote)

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: כֹּל שֶׁפּוֹסֵל וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says: Whoever disqualifies, etc.
phrases.notes: The full line in the משנה is: whoever disqualifies others also disqualifies himself, and whoever does not disqualify others does not disqualify himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: כֹּל שֶׁפּוֹסֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New section; returns to the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whoever disqualifies others also disqualifies himself, and whoever does not disqualify others does not disqualify himself.

steps.title: What does רבי יוסי mean
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי יוסי's rule is actually saying.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is רבי יוסי saying?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what רבי יוסי means. This sets up the guesses that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי's rule is short and general. The גמרא needs to know which case in the משנה it refers to, and how it differs from the תנא קמא.

phrases.english: What is Rabbi Yosei saying?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי קָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the rule quoted in step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which case does רבי יוסי address, and what is his point?

steps.title: A first guess: the brother-in-law case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts a first guess. In the תנא קמא's case where his wife and brother-in-law went overseas, the brother-in-law's wife is forbidden, but his own wife is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it refers to what the תנא קמא said, where his wife and his brother-in-law went overseas, so the wife of his brother-in-law is forbidden, and his own wife is permitted...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a possible answer by pointing to a case of the תנא קמא. The sentence is not finished yet; step 10 completes it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אילימא opens a guess that the גמרא usually goes on to challenge. The case: he sinned with his wife's sister, who is married to his brother-in-law. She becomes forbidden to her husband, but his own wife stays permitted to him. The guess is that רבי יוסי is reacting to this case.

keyTerms.meaning: The first, unnamed opinion in the משנה

phrases.english: If we say that the first tanna said,
that his wife and his brother-in-law went overseas,
the wife of his brother-in-law is forbidden,
phrases.notes: She is his wife's sister. Because he was with her, she becomes forbidden to her own husband.

phrases.english: and his own wife is permitted,

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא דְּקָאָמַר תַּנָּא קַמָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a first possible answer to step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A tentative suggestion that רבי יוסי refers to the brother-in-law case. Step 10 finishes it and step 11 tests it.

steps.title: First guess finished: both women permitted
steps.stepSummary: In the first guess, רבי יוסי tells the תנא קמא that since the man's own wife is permitted, his brother-in-law's wife should be permitted too.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to this guess, רבי יוסי says to the תנא קמא: just as his own wife is permitted, the wife of his brother-in-law is also permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes its first guess about רבי יוסי's rule. The תנא קמא forbade only the brother-in-law's wife, and רבי יוסי says she should be permitted just like the man's own wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא treated the two women differently. In this guess, רבי יוסי says they should be treated the same, and the shared result is 'permitted.' The direction of his reasoning runs from his own wife to the other man's wife.

keyTerms.meaning: And he says to him (here, רבי יוסי answering the תנא קמא)
His brother-in-law (here, the husband of his wife's sister)

phrases.english: And רבי יוסי says to him:
phrases.notes: 'Him' is the תנא קמא, the first opinion in the משנה.

phrases.english: Just as his wife is permitted,
the wife of his brother-in-law is also permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְקָאָמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: כִּי הֵיכִי דְּאִשְׁתּוֹ שַׁרְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the first guess begun in step 9 by giving רבי יוסי's response.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יוסי means that both women are permitted, because his own wife is permitted.

steps.title: The first guess reverses the wording of the rule
steps.stepSummary: If that were רבי יוסי's point, his rule should have been worded the other way around: whoever does not disqualify himself does not disqualify others.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, instead of saying 'whoever does not disqualify others does not disqualify himself,' he should have said 'whoever does not disqualify himself does not disqualify others.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the first guess. It does not match the order of the words in רבי יוסי's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first guess, the reasoning starts from the man himself (his wife is permitted) and moves to others (so the brother-in-law's wife is permitted too). A rule built on that idea would begin with 'himself' and end with 'others.' רבי יוסי's actual wording goes the opposite way, so the guess cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: Disqualifies (makes a woman forbidden to her husband)

keyTerms.term: עַל יְדֵי אֲחֵרִים / עַל יְדֵי עַצְמוֹ

phrases.english: If so,

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל שֶׁאֵין פּוֹסֵל עַל יְדֵי אֲחֵרִים —
phrases.english: [instead of] 'whoever does not disqualify others'
'does not disqualify himself,'

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁאֵין פּוֹסֵל עַל יְדֵי עַצְמוֹ —
phrases.english: 'whoever does not disqualify himself'
'does not disqualify others'
is what he should have said!
phrases.notes: 'Himself' means his own wife becoming forbidden to him; 'others' means the brother-in-law's wife becoming forbidden to her husband.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the first guess in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The first guess, that רבי יוסי permits both women.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The guess reasons from 'himself' to 'others,' but רבי יוסי's wording puts 'others' first and 'himself' second.

steps.title: Second guess: both women forbidden
steps.stepSummary: Instead, maybe רבי יוסי means that just as the brother-in-law's wife is forbidden, the man's own wife is also forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: But rather: just as the wife of his brother-in-law is forbidden, his own wife is also forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a second guess. It reads רבי יוסי the opposite way: both women are forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This guess also treats the two women the same, but the shared result is now 'forbidden.' The reasoning moves from others (the brother-in-law's wife) to himself (his own wife). That matches the order of 'כל הפוסל על ידי אחרים פוסל על ידי עצמו.'

phrases.aramaic: וְאֶלָּא כִּי הֵיכִי דְּאֵשֶׁת גִּיסוֹ אֲסִירָא —
phrases.english: But rather: just as the wife of his brother-in-law is forbidden,
his wife is also forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא כִּי הֵיכִי דְּאֵשֶׁת גִּיסוֹ אֲסִירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the first guess, which failed in step 11, with the opposite reading.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יוסי means that both women are forbidden, because the brother-in-law's wife is forbidden.

steps.title: The second half of the rule has no job
steps.stepSummary: The second guess explains 'whoever disqualifies,' but the clause 'whoever does not disqualify' would then have no purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for 'whoever disqualifies.' But 'whoever does not disqualify': what is it doing here?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the second guess. It explains only the first half of רבי יוסי's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי יוסי only meant to forbid both women, the clause 'whoever disqualifies others disqualifies himself' would be enough. The second clause, about someone who does not disqualify, has no case to apply to. So this guess leaves part of the משנה with nothing to do.

keyTerms.meaning: This works well for (introduces 'but there is still a problem')
What is it doing here? (what purpose does it serve)

phrases.english: This works well for 'whoever disqualifies,'
but 'whoever does not disqualify': what is it doing here?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתִינַח ״כֹּל שֶׁפּוֹסֵל״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the second guess in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The second guess, that רבי יוסי forbids both women.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That reading accounts only for the first clause, so the second clause of the rule would be useless.

steps.title: רבי אמי: the rule goes back to the first משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי says רבי יוסי's rule refers to the opening משנה of the פרק: a woman who remarried by permission of the בית דין leaves and brings no קרבן, while one who remarried based on עדים alone leaves and must bring a קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי said: the rule refers to the first part of the פרק. If she remarried by permission of the בית דין, she must leave and is exempt from a קרבן. If she remarried based on witnesses, she must leave and is obligated to bring a קרבן. The power of the בית דין is greater, since it exempts her from the קרבן.
steps.whatsHappening: Since both guesses failed, רבי אמי gives a new answer. He links רבי יוסי's rule to the difference between marrying by permission of the בית דין and marrying based only on עדים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first משנה of the פרק teaches that permission from the בית דין changes the outcome: she still must leave, but she is exempt from a קרבן. רבי אמי will use this difference between בית דין and עדים to give both halves of רבי יוסי's rule a real case.

keyTerms.meaning: On the first part (the opening משנה of the פרק)
Based on witnesses (without the court's permission)

phrases.english: רבי אמי said: [it refers] to the first part:
phrases.notes: He means the very first משנה of this פרק, about a woman told that her husband died overseas.

phrases.aramaic: נִיסֵּת עַל פִּי בֵּית דִּין — תֵּצֵא,
phrases.english: If she married by permission of the court, she must leave
and is exempt from an offering.
If based on witnesses, she must leave
and is obligated to bring an offering.
The power of the court is greater,
since it exempts her from the offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי אַרֵישָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the second guess fails in step 13, רבי אמי gives a new answer to the question in step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יוסי's rule is built on the difference between remarriage by permission of the בית דין and remarriage based on עדים, taken from the first משנה.

steps.title: How the תנא קמא sees the case in רבי אמי's reading
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי אמי, the תנא קמא says it makes no difference whether she married based on עדים, where the brother-in-law's wife is permitted, or by permission of the בית דין, where she is forbidden. In both cases his own wife stays permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the תנא קמא says: it is no different if it was based on witnesses, where the wife of his brother-in-law is permitted, and no different if it was by permission of the court, where the wife of his brother-in-law is forbidden. Either way, his own wife is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי lays out the תנא קמא's view using the בית דין versus עדים difference. This sets up רבי יוסי's disagreement, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the תנא קמא, what happens to the brother-in-law's wife depends on how she remarried: based on עדים she is permitted, but by permission of the בית דין she is forbidden. Even so, the man's own wife is not affected in either case. The two different results for 'others' are what will let both halves of רבי יוסי's rule have a real case.

keyTerms.meaning: The first, unnamed opinion in the משנה

phrases.english: And the first tanna says:
it is no different if based on witnesses,
where the wife of his brother-in-law is permitted,

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא שְׁנָא עַל פִּי בֵּית דִּין,
phrases.english: and it is no different if by permission of the court,
where the wife of his brother-in-law is forbidden.
phrases.notes: The גמרא leaves the ending unsaid: in both cases, his own wife stays permitted to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְקָאָמַר תַּנָּא קַמָּא: לָא שְׁנָא עַל פִּי עֵדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רבי אמי's distinction from step 14 to the תנא קמא's ruling.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: For the תנא קמא, the brother-in-law's wife is permitted after remarrying based on עדים and forbidden after remarrying by permission of the בית דין, but the man's own wife is permitted either way.

steps.title: רבי אמי finishes: how רבי יוסי answers the תנא קמא
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי אמי, רבי יוסי says that when she remarried by permission of the בית דין, the brother-in-law's wife is forbidden, so the man's own wife is forbidden too. When she remarried based on עדים, the brother-in-law's wife is permitted, so his own wife is permitted too.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוסי says to him: When it was by permission of the בית דין, he disqualifies others, so he disqualifies himself. When it was based on עדים, he does not disqualify others, so he does not disqualify himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רבי אמי's explanation by giving רבי יוסי's side of the argument against the תנא קמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי links the two women together. If the brother-in-law's wife becomes forbidden, which happens when the בית דין gave permission, then the man's own wife is forbidden as well. If the brother-in-law's wife stays permitted, which happens when only עדים testified, then his own wife stays permitted. This way both halves of רבי יוסי's rule have a purpose, which answers the problem raised in step 13.

keyTerms.meaning: disqualifies others (makes another man's wife forbidden to him)
disqualifies himself (his own wife becomes forbidden to him)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אמי's reading: the בית דין case means both wives are forbidden. The עדים case means both wives are permitted. רבי יוסי makes the man's own wife follow the brother-in-law's wife.

phrases.english: And רבי יוסי says to him:
phrases.notes: "Him" is the תנא קמא, the first opinion in the משנה.

phrases.aramaic: עַל פִּי בֵּית דִּין, דְּפוֹסֵל עַל יְדֵי אֲחֵרִים
phrases.english: By permission of the court, where he disqualifies others
he disqualifies himself.

phrases.aramaic: עַל פִּי עֵדִים, דְּאֵינוֹ פּוֹסֵל עַל יְדֵי אֲחֵרִים
phrases.english: Based on witnesses, where he does not disqualify others
he does not disqualify himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְקָאָמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: עַל פִּי בֵּית דִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי אמי's reading by giving רבי יוסי's reply to the תנא קמא's view from step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יוסי's rule means that the man's own wife follows the status of the brother-in-law's wife: forbidden in the בית דין case, permitted in the עדים case.

steps.title: רבי יצחק נפחא: the rule refers to the later clause
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק נפחא offers a different reading. רבי יוסי is talking about the later clause of the משנה, and the difference is whether it was the man's betrothed or his full wife who went away with the brother-in-law. The תנא קמא holds that either way the brother-in-law's wife is forbidden and the man's own wife is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק נפחא said: Really, it refers to the later clause. One case is where his betrothed and his brother-in-law went away. The other case is where his wife and his brother-in-law went away. And the תנא קמא says: It makes no difference whether it was his wife and brother-in-law or his betrothed and brother-in-law. The brother-in-law's wife is forbidden, and his own wife is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: A new אמורא, רבי יצחק נפחא, gives a different explanation of what רבי יוסי's rule is about. Here he first lays out the two cases and the view of the תנא קמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אמי tied the rule to the opening משנה, which is about בית דין versus עדים. רבי יצחק נפחא instead ties it to the later clause about the brother-in-law. He splits that clause into two cases: the man's full wife went away, or only his ארוסה (betrothed) went away. The תנא קמא makes no distinction: in both cases the brother-in-law's wife is forbidden and the man's own woman stays permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: really, actually; introduces the speaker's own reading
the later clause of a משנה

steps.confusionAlert: Keep the two women apart. 'His wife' or 'his betrothed' is the man's own woman. 'The brother-in-law's wife' is the woman this man married by mistake.

phrases.english: רבי יצחק נפחא said:
Actually, it refers to the later clause
(This is where he married his brother-in-law's wife,
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets. The explanation goes with the wording that comes right after them.

phrases.english: and that is where he married his brother-in-law's betrothed.)
This is where his betrothed and his brother-in-law went away,
that is where his wife and his brother-in-law went away,
and the first תנא says:
It makes no difference whether his wife and brother-in-law,
and it makes no difference whether his betrothed and brother-in-law;
his brother-in-law's wife is forbidden, and his own wife is permitted,

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יִצְחָק נַפָּחָא אָמַר: לְעוֹלָם אַסֵּיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to the problem from steps 11-13, different from רבי אמי's answer in steps 14-16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יוסי's rule is about the later clause, and it separates a full wife from a betrothed. The תנא קמא treats both the same.

steps.title: רבי יצחק נפחא: רבי יוסי splits wife from betrothed
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי יצחק נפחא, רבי יוסי says the following. With a full wife, nobody can claim there was a condition on the marriage, so the brother-in-law's wife is not disqualified and neither is his own wife. With a betrothed, people could claim the קידושין had a condition, so the brother-in-law's wife is disqualified, and his own betrothed is disqualified too.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוסי says to him: His wife and brother-in-law: one cannot say he had a condition in the marriage. So since he does not disqualify the other man, he does not disqualify himself. His betrothed and brother-in-law: one can say he had a condition in the betrothal. So since he disqualifies others, he also disqualifies himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רבי יצחק נפחא's explanation by giving רבי יוסי's answer to the תנא קמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key idea is whether people might say there was a תנאי (condition). A full marriage (נישואין) is not usually thought to hang on a condition. So everyone sees that the mistaken second marriage meant nothing, and nobody becomes forbidden. A betrothal (קידושין) could be thought to have had a condition. Then the brother-in-law's wife becomes forbidden, and by רבי יוסי's rule the man's betrothed becomes forbidden too.

keyTerms.meaning: a condition attached to a marriage or betrothal
betrothal, the first stage of marriage

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יצחק נפחא's reading: with a full wife, both women are permitted. With a betrothed, both are forbidden, because people might think the קידושין had a תנאי.

phrases.english: And רבי יוסי says to him:
His wife and his brother-in-law,
where one cannot say
that he had a condition in the marriage,
since he does not disqualify another
he does not disqualify himself.
His betrothed and his brother-in-law,
where one can say
that he had a condition in the betrothal,
and so he disqualifies others
he also disqualifies himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְקָאָמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: אִשְׁתּוֹ וְגִיסוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי יצחק נפחא's reading by giving רבי יוסי's reply to the תנא קמא's view from step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: With a full wife, nobody is disqualified, since no condition can be suspected. With a betrothed, both women are disqualified, since a condition on the קידושין can be suspected.

steps.title: שמואל rules like רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה reports that שמואל ruled the הלכה follows רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said that שמואל said: The הלכה follows רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a practical ruling: according to שמואל, we follow רבי יוסי's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After explaining what רבי יוסי meant, the גמרא now records that שמואל decided the הלכה like him. This ruling sets up the next step, where רב יוסף will question whether שמואל could really have said this.

keyTerms.meaning: רב יהודה reporting in the name of his teacher שמואל

phrases.english: רב יהודה said that שמואל said:
The הלכה follows רבי יוסי.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from explaining רבי יוסי's view to a ruling that the הלכה follows him.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to שמואל, the הלכה follows רבי יוסי: whoever disqualifies others disqualifies himself.

steps.title: רב יוסף questions whether שמואל said this
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף asks whether שמואל could really have ruled like רבי יוסי. He points to a known argument: רב says a יבמה is like a married woman, and שמואל says she is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף objects: Did שמואל really say this? But it was stated: about a יבמה, רב said she is like a married woman, and שמואל said she is not like a married woman.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף starts a challenge against the claim that שמואל ruled like רבי יוסי. He brings in a separate argument between רב and שמואל about a יבמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף wants to show that שמואל's view about a יבמה does not fit with ruling like רבי יוסי. At this point he has only quoted the argument. The case it applies to comes in the next step, and the full contradiction is spelled out after that.

keyTerms.meaning: a widow waiting for יבום from her late husband's brother

phrases.english: רב יוסף strongly objects to this:
And did שמואל really say this?
But wasn't it stated: a יבמה,

phrases.aramaic: רַב אָמַר: הֲרֵי הִיא כְּאֵשֶׁת אִישׁ,
phrases.english: רב said: she is like a married woman,
and שמואל said: she is not like a married woman.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב יוֹסֵף: וּמִי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ruling in step 19 that שמואל holds like רבי יוסי.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's report that שמואל ruled like רבי יוסי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל's known view elsewhere, that a יבמה is not like a married woman, seems not to fit with ruling like רבי יוסי.

steps.title: רב הונא describes the case of the יבמה argument
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא explains the case where רב and שמואל argue. A brother betrothed a woman and went overseas. The man left behind heard that his brother had died, and he went ahead and married his brother's wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב הונא said: For example, where his brother betrothed a woman and went off overseas, and he heard that his brother had died, and he went ahead and married his wife.
steps.whatsHappening: This is still part of רב יוסף's challenge. רב הונא's explanation spells out the exact case of the רב-שמואל argument, so the contradiction with רבי יוסי can be shown next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is about someone who married his brother's wife after a report that the brother had died. Like the cases in our משנה, it is a marriage based on a mistaken report of death. That is why it can be compared with רבי יוסי's rule. The גמרא will finish the challenge in the next lines.

keyTerms.meaning: for example; in a case where

phrases.english: And רב הונא said:
For example, where his brother betrothed a woman,
and went off overseas,
and he heard that his brother had died,
phrases.notes: "He" is the brother who stayed home.

phrases.english: and he went ahead and married his wife.
phrases.notes: "His wife" means the missing brother's wife, taken in יבום.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב הוּנָא: כְּגוֹן שֶׁקִּדֵּשׁ אָחִיו אֶת הָאִשָּׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the case of the רב-שמואל argument quoted in step 20, building רב יוסף's challenge.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: By pinning down the case of the יבמה argument, רב יוסף prepares to show that שמואל's view there conflicts with ruling like רבי יוסי.

steps.title: רב forbids her, שמואל permits her
steps.stepSummary: רב says the betrothed woman who was mistakenly married by her brother-in-law is like a married woman and is forbidden to the יבם. שמואל says she is not like a married woman and is permitted to him. This finishes רב יוסף's challenge.
steps.simpleTranslation: For רב said: she is like a married woman and is forbidden to the יבם. And שמואל said: she is not like a married woman, and she is permitted to him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes laying out the argument between רב and שמואל that רב יוסף brought up. שמואל permits the betrothed woman, and that is the point of the challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Following רבי יצחק נפחא's reading, רבי יוסי disqualifies a betrothed woman because people might say the קידושין had a condition. Yet here שמואל permits a betrothed woman and does not worry about that. So how could שמואל have ruled like רבי יוסי?

keyTerms.meaning: Brother-in-law; here it refers to her original husband

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'יבם' does not mean the brother who married her. It means her original husband, the one who went overseas.

phrases.english: For Rav said:
she is like a married woman
and is forbidden to the yavam,
phrases.notes: Here this means her first husband. He gets called the יבם because his brother married her.

phrases.english: and Shmuel said:
she is not like a married woman,
and she is permitted to him!

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּרַב אָמַר: הֲרֵי הִיא כְּאֵשֶׁת אִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the case רב הונא described by giving the two rulings, which completes רב יוסף's challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's report that שמואל ruled like רבי יוסי (step 19)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל permits a betrothed woman in this case and does not worry that people will suspect a conditional קידושין. But רבי יוסי (according to רבי יצחק נפחא) disqualifies a betrothed woman because of exactly that worry.

steps.title: Maybe שמואל meant רבי אמי's reading of רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks רב יוסף how he knows שמואל meant רבי יוסי as רבי יצחק נפחא explained him. Maybe שמואל meant רבי יוסי as רבי אמי explained him.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: And how do you know that when שמואל said 'the הלכה follows רבי יוסי,' he was talking about רבי יצחק נפחא's reading? Maybe he was talking about רבי אמי's reading!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on רב יוסף's challenge. He says שמואל may have been agreeing with a different explanation of רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two ways to understand רבי יוסי. In רבי אמי's way, the 'condition on the קידושין' worry never comes up. If שמואל followed רבי אמי's reading, then there is no clash with שמואל permitting the betrothed woman.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
And from where do you know that when Shmuel said
"the halacha follows Rabbi Yosei"
he was speaking about Rabbi Yitzchak Nappacha's reading?
Perhaps he was speaking about Rabbi Ami's reading!
phrases.notes: This is רבי אמי's earlier explanation of רבי יוסי. For him the difference is marrying with בית דין's permission versus marrying because of witnesses.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: וּמִמַּאי דְּכִי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יוסף's challenge by questioning which reading of רבי יוסי שמואל agreed with.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the assumption behind רב יוסף's challenge. It does not reject שמואל's ruling itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב יוסף assumed שמואל endorsed רבי יצחק נפחא's reading, but שמואל may have endorsed רבי אמי's reading, which has no clash.

steps.title: Even with רבי יצחק נפחא's reading, which clause did שמואל mean?
steps.stepSummary: אביי adds a second point. Even if שמואל meant רבי יצחק נפחא's reading, how do we know he was ruling on the part where רבי יוסי says the woman is 'disqualified'? The sentence continues in the next lines.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even if he was talking about רבי יצחק נפחא's reading, how do you know he meant the part about 'disqualifies'?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי opens a second, backup answer. This line sets up the next move, which finishes his point in the following text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי's statement (per רבי יצחק נפחא) has two parts: the full wife is not disqualified, and the betrothed is disqualified. שמואל might have been ruling only on the part that does not disqualify. Then he would not clash with permitting the betrothed woman.

keyTerms.meaning: And even if; introduces a second, fallback point

phrases.english: And even if it was about Rabbi Yitzchak Nappacha's reading,
from where do you know that it was about "disqualifies",
phrases.notes: This points to רבי יוסי's words about the betrothed case, where he says she is disqualified. אביי's sentence finishes in the next lines.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי נָמֵי אַדְּרַבִּי יִצְחָק נַפָּחָא, מִמַּאי דְּאַ״פּוֹסֵל״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, fallback answer to רב יוסף. It still works even if we accept that שמואל meant רבי יצחק נפחא's reading.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that שמואל's ruling must cover the 'disqualifies' part of רבי יוסי's words.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב יוסף assumed שמואל agreed with every part of רבי יוסי's statement. He may have agreed with only the part that does not disqualify.
